chapter: Club Alabam and the Europe contract
title: Arthur Lyons brings in a European impresario
summary: Lyons introduces the Russian impresario Lenidow, who wants a band and a show, and cast members for Europe are found.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And then one day Lyons come in and said to me, "How would you like to go to Europe?" I looked at him as if to say, "Are you kidding?" He said no, I've got a man, an impresario from Europe. A man named Leonidoff. Not the one in Radio City. This was, he spelled his name -L-e-n-i-d-o-w, which is the same thing. W is double f in Russian, see? And they were Russian, see.

Now, so I said, (unintelligible), and he'll be in here at ten o'clock tonight. Lyons got there first to prepare us so the boys would be all in shape. Well, one thing we only had one fellow drank a lot, a little bit. That was our trombone player. He would only drink when you started talking
to him about home and things like that. He was from Baltimore, and he would start drinking.

So I'll tell you about him after, but let me tell you about this show. Lyons brought this man in and this man heard us and he said, "I think that's what we need. But we've got to have a show." And Lyons said, "Don't worry about that, because I've got a choreographer here. Charles Davis can do that. And all he had to find was the necessary people. And we found some people like Adelaide Hall, Margaret Simms. And Eddie Rector didn't want to go, and neither did Johnny Higgins, see. So, we found others to take their places. Greenlee & Drayton was a big act in vaudeville then, see. And there was some others. Arthur Bryson. So we had a good show. So that was the way it was.
